script: In 1959, the two most powerful men on Earth nearly came to blows inside a fake kitchen. America had built a model home in the middle of Moscow, and swore that any ordinary American worker could afford every machine inside it. Soviet leader Khrushchev called it a lie, a propaganda trick stuffed with machines that did not exist. Vice President Nixon fired back, jabbing a finger into Khrushchev's chest while the cameras rolled. Khrushchev jabbed right back, promising to show America Kuzka's mother, a threat his own translators could not explain. But here is the part nobody mentions, a Pepsi executive was waiting in that crowd with a plan of his own. He steered the furious Khrushchev into drinking Pepsi in front of every photographer in Moscow, the exact photo his company had chased for months. That single staged sip grew into an exclusive Soviet deal, and when Moscow ran short of cash, it paid Pepsi in warships. Seventeen submarines, a cruiser, a frigate and a destroyer, all traded away for soda syrup. For one strange moment a soda company controlled a navy, and it all started with an argument in a fake kitchen.
